title: Vector triangles for coplanar equilibrium practice

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct retrieval of the two equilibrium conditions, three diagnostic choices about closure and direction, a perpendicular geometry construction, an oblique component solution, then a mixed moments and force-triangle rigid-body problem

visual_planning.reason: Three later structured questions benefit from learner-visible direction scaffolds. No assets are claimed in this deterministic four-file package.

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, values, wording and figure briefs are original. The official evidence grounds closed scale triangles, equilibrium conditions and the moments-to-force workflow without supplying any copied scenario or numerical data.

questions.prompt: From the previous lesson, state the two independent conditions that must both be satisfied for a rigid body to be in equilibrium.
Three coplanar forces act on a small ring. Which vector construction shows that their resultant force is zero?

options.A: The three arrows are drawn from one common tail and have equal lengths.
options.B: The three arrows are placed head-to-tail and the final head returns to the first tail.
options.C: The two largest arrows are parallel and the third arrow is perpendicular to them.
options.D: The three force magnitudes add to zero without using their directions.

questions.prompt: A closed force triangle has already been drawn correctly. Which change is allowed without changing the physical forces represented?

options.A: Reverse one arrow so that its head becomes its tail.
options.B: Rotate one arrow until the triangle looks right-angled.
options.C: Redraw the three unchanged arrows in a different cyclic head-to-tail order.
options.D: Shorten the largest arrow so that all three sides are equal.

questions.prompt: Three force arrows form a closed triangle. What can be concluded from that triangle alone?

options.A: The resultant force is zero, but the resultant torque still needs a separate check for an extended body.
options.B: Both resultant force and resultant torque must be zero for every possible arrangement of the forces.
options.C: The object must be at rest and cannot be moving at constant velocity.
options.D: All three forces must have the same magnitude.

questions.prompt: A small ring is in equilibrium under three coplanar forces. Two forces are 36 N east and 48 N north. The third force is P.

figure.purpose: Provide a clean blank drawing area with east and north reference directions for the learner's force triangle.
figure.brief: Landscape black-and-white question diagram on pure white. Show only a small origin marker, a short east reference arrow, a short north reference arrow and generous blank space. Do not draw any force side or reveal P.
figure.alt_text: A blank force-triangle workspace with east and north reference directions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using a scale of 1.0 cm to represent 12 N, draw a labelled closed vector triangle for the three forces.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the direction of P, giving the angle from west.

questions.prompt: A ring is held in equilibrium by three coplanar forces. Force A is 50 N east. Force B is 80 N at 60 degrees north of west. Force C is unknown.

figure.purpose: Make the two known force directions unambiguous while leaving the unknown force entirely for the learner.
figure.brief: Landscape black-and-white question diagram on pure white. Show a central ring, a 50 N east arrow labelled A and an 80 N arrow labelled B at 60 degrees north of west. Include a small horizontal reference and angle arc. Do not draw force C or any components.
figure.alt_text: A ring with a 50 newton east force and an 80 newton force directed 60 degrees north of west.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine the east-west and north-south components of the combined force A plus B. State each direction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Hence calculate the magnitude of C.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the direction of C, giving the acute angle from south.

questions.prompt: A uniform horizontal beam of length 1.2 m and weight 240 N is hinged to a wall at its left end. A cable attached to the right end pulls at 30 degrees above the horizontal. The beam is in equilibrium. The hinge exerts a force R on the beam.

figure.purpose: Show the beam geometry and force locations needed for the prior moment calculation without revealing the reaction direction.
figure.brief: Landscape black-and-white question diagram on pure white. Draw a 1.2 m horizontal beam hinged at the left, a 240 N downward weight at the midpoint and a cable at the right end directed 30 degrees above the beam towards the wall. Label the cable tension T. Indicate an unknown hinge force R only by its label beside the hinge, with no arrow direction.
figure.alt_text: A horizontal hinged beam has a midpoint weight and an angled supporting cable, with an unknown hinge force.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use moments about the hinge to calculate the tension T in the cable.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Draw a labelled closed vector triangle for the weight, cable tension and hinge force acting on the beam.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the force triangle or components to determine the magnitude and direction of R.
